statement: Pharloom is structured as an immense vertical spire ascending from subterranean moss to mountain peaks.
The Lower Depths encompass Moss Grotto, Bonebottom shantytown, The Marrow bone mines, and Deep Docks.
The Middle Threshold encompasses Greymoor moors, the bronze Belltower, and the toxic Bile Lake.
The Summit Metropolis encompasses Gilded City, High Citadel, Choral Chambers, and Peak of Song.
Pharloom's governance is acoustic, structured around song, choral liturgies, and resonant bronze bells.
The musical score features liturgical pipe organs, brass carillons, and choral polyphony in the Citadel.
Massive bronze bells serve as industrial shift alarms and ideological instruments of disorientation.
Lower classes endure brutal labor in the bone furnaces to cast the bells and spires that oppress them.
The High Citadel casts toxic industrial pollutants and chemical runoff downward into Bile Lake.
Ringing bells create intangible acoustic walls that compel pilgrim movement while suppressing rebellion.
Whether the song of Pharloom was originally a communal harvest chant before theocracy is an open debate.
The foundational masonry of the Belltower pre-dates the current theocratic Citadel hierarchy.
Hornet is captured and transported toward Pharloom in an armored carriage by masked guards.
Hornet is held in an iron cage bound with heavy magical silk threads to suppress her powers.
Glowing butterfly spirits ambush the caravan on the entrance bridge, creating a breach for Hornet.
Hornet shatters her cage with a burst of thread, rupturing the bridge and causing the carriage to fall.
Hornet falls thousands of feet into the subterranean damp caverns of Moss Grotto.
Hornet awakens on the cavern floor stripped of her silk spools, advanced tools, and full strength.
Hornet defeats the Moss Mother in her nest and ascends to the refugee shantytown of Bonebottom.

statement: Pharloom authorities possessed specific intelligence regarding Hornet's royal Hallownest lineage.
Hornet's ability reset represents somatic trauma from prolonged binding and a catastrophic fall.
Hornet immediately chooses to ascend Pharloom to confront her captors rather than seeking retreat.
Whether the butterflies that ambushed the convoy were wild spirits or rebel Weaver scouts is unconfirmed.
The physical geographic distance between Hallownest and Pharloom spans vast barren outer wastes.
Grand Mother Silk is the supreme Weaver sovereign presiding at the summit Peak of Song in Pharloom.
Grand Mother Silk presides over the monumental Loom of Pharloom, weaving reality and theocratic order.
Silk operates as an active, tactile metaphysical and structural force across Pharloom.
Unlike ethereal Soul, Silk is a physical protein biopolymer spun from glands and harvested from chitin.
In-game silk spinning reflects liquid crystalline phase transitions in real spider silk biopolymers.
Grand Mother Silk weaves golden liturgical threads that bind pilgrims into thralls (Puppet-Pilgrims).
In the climax, Grand Mother Silk unleashes multi-layered thread waves, spools, and choral fugues.
Grand Mother Silk sustains her power through systemic metabolic extraction of pilgrim life energy.
Silk serves as an embodied metaphor for social entanglement, debt servitude, and theocratic binding.
Hornet reclaims and unpicks these liturgical threads, weaponizing the material of oppression.
Whether Grand Mother Silk was an ancient contemporary of the Wyrms remains a historical open question.
The Black Thread in deepest vaults represents corrupted silk or a synthesis of silk and Void matter.
The Weavers of Hallownest's Deepnest originated ancestrally within the soaring kingdom of Pharloom.
The Weavers' Cradle was the sacred ancestral sanctuary where Weavers spun silk from ancient spindles.
Weaver mythology reveres the First Weaver as the mythological progenitor who spun the first thread.
A major schism erupted when the Citadel centralized silk production into the grand Loom of Pharloom.
Dissident Weavers undertook the Great Migration across the wastes to settle in Hallownest's Deepnest.

statement: Surviving Weavers like the hermit Eva and the Weaver Elder persist in secluded sanctuaries in Pharloom.

statement: Eva recognizes Hornet as Herrah's daughter and heir to Weavers, teaching her ancient threadcraft.
Hornet must confront the Sister of the Loom and spectral threaded phantoms in ancestral trials.
The Weavers represent an artisanal guild whose indigenous craft was co-opted by industrial theocracy.
The migration to Deepnest was an anti-imperial exodus choosing darkness over theocratic slavery.
Hornet's journey through Pharloom is an archaeological reclamation of her maternal Weaver heritage.
Whether any Weavers returned to Pharloom after Hallownest fell remains an open historical question.
The High Citadel is an immense metropolis of white marble spires and clockwork vaults at Pharloom's summit.
The Citadel operates as the theocratic center ruled by clergy under the authority of Grand Mother Silk.
The Great Pilgrimage invites bugs upward toward the Citadel with the promise of divine musical absolution.
Pilgrims like Sherma chant sacred hymns and offer strings of Rosary beads at roadside shrines.
In the Choral Chambers, the Choir Master leads congregations in synchronized liturgical singing.
Hymns are amplified by massive mechanical pipe organs routed directly into the mountain bedrock.
Pilgrims reaching upper gates are stripped of wealth and forced into mines or bound as Puppet-Pilgrims.
The promise of salvation is cynically deployed to justify systemic somatic exploitation of pilgrims.
Religious devotion is monetized: prayer beads serve simultaneously as sacred offerings, currency, and ammo.
Synchronized choral singing functions as crowd control, inducing hypnotic compliance across worshippers.
Whether the high clergy believe their own dogma or act as cynical technocrats is an open question.
Pilgrims reaching the apex loom were converted into consecrated silk unguents to fuel the grand loom.
Lace serves as Hornet's primary martial rival and theatrical foil across Pharloom.
Lace wears a white silk cloak, wields a slender rapier needle, and first battles Hornet in Deep Docks.
Lace executes acrobatic forward thrusts, backflips, parrying counter-stances, and downward lunges.
Lace's battle theme features syncopated pizzicato strings and playful violin runs mirroring her swordsmanship.
Following defeats, Lace retreats with theatrical applause, reappearing to mock Hornet's mission.
In the High Citadel, Hornet clashes with Lace in a second, more lethal duel with gilded thread barriers.
In deep chasm depths, Hornet confronts Lost Lace, a corrupted variant bound by dark twisting threads.
Lace is an essential psychological foil: flamboyant and nihilistic where Hornet is solemn and duty-bound.
Their duels feature articulate banter and mutual respect, inverting the silent duels of the original game.
Lace's corruption into Lost Lace proves that cynical detachment cannot protect against theocratic power.
Whether Lace was spun artificially from Weaver silk or survived an ancient noble house is unconfirmed.
The bond between Hornet and Lace spans rivalrous martial respect and deep emotional intimacy.
The Last Judge is an immense, golden-masked judicial executor guarding the gate to the High Citadel.
The Last Judge wears ceremonial vestments, a spiked crown, and a stylized golden death mask.
In battle, the Last Judge wields a massive bronze gavel and unleashes punishing waves of sacred fire.

statement: The boss encounter requires mastering diagonal dive kicks and mid-air tool deployment to survive.
Defeating the Last Judge permits passage past the grand portcullis into the Gilded City.
The trial is an execution gauntlet designed to admit only the most resilient pilgrims into the Citadel.
The Last Judge embodies sovereign exception: justice grounded purely in monopoly on lethal violence.
The golden mask strips the executor of personal face and name, serving as an unfeeling divine instrument.
The judge's sacred flames are fed by incinerating heretical manuscripts and rejected pilgrim offerings.
Whether the Judge was a mortal who ascended through obedience or a clockwork construct is debated.
Tablets near the gate hint at previous judges slain by rebels, indicating an office rather than an immortal individual.
The executioner at the promised gate shatters the benevolent illusion of Pharloom's musical paradise.
The Marrow is a subterranean industrial zone filled with bone pulverizers, furnaces, and smoke.
The Marrow mines and processes fossilized insect bone, calcified chitin, and mineralized shell shards.
Laborers in The Marrow are overseen by brutal supervisors like the Iron Warden wielding tongs and slag.
Pilgrims lacking Rosary funds are routed into bone furnaces under the pretext of penitential service.
Sherma is a devout, clumsy pilgrim dressed in burlap who wanders through hazardous mining shafts.
Hornet repeatedly rescues Sherma from industrial beasts, collapsing scaffolds, and furnace pits.
Weary miners like Drudge recount the tolling of shift bells and the deadly conditions in the pits.
The spires and bronze bells of the Citadel are physically constructed from bone and shells mined in the Marrow.
Religious ideology recasts exhaustion and physical injury as marks of holy martyrdom and cleansing.
Sherma's unshakeable devotion critiques false consciousness: revering the system that grinds him down.
Whether an organized underground resistance exists in The Marrow remains an unresolved plot thread.
Colossal fossilized bones in cavern walls suggest giant prehistoric mega-insects preceded the kingdom.
Pharloom's economy operates through a commercial network centered around Gilded City and guild outposts.
Currency is denominated in Rosary Beads, perforated prayer beads strung on thread or used as ammunition.
Hornet drops unstrung Rosaries on death, but can protect them by stringing them onto cords at benches.
In The Marrow, Hornet encounters the Bell Beast, an enormous multi-legged armored transport behemoth.
The Bell Beast was enslaved through heavy ringing bronze bells clamped around its neck, attacking in a frenzy.
Severing its bell collar frees the beast to serve as Hornet's fast-travel transit across subterranean bellways.
In Gilded City, wealthy merchants exchange rare needle alloys and tools for heavy strings of Rosaries.
The Forge-Daughter and Pinstress provide weapon upgrades and tool crafting, showing independent craft culture.
The transit network reveals industrialization achieved through the violent subjugation of native megafauna.
The Rosary economy illustrates the fusion of religion and capitalism: prayer is literal currency.
Liberating the Bell Beast substitutes theocratic acoustic coercion with mutual interspecies respect.
Whether wild herds of Bell Beasts still roam outer crags remains an unchronicled ecological detail.
Silksong is structured around a three-act narrative progression organizing physical vertical ascent.
Act I (The Lower Ascent) spans Moss Grotto, Bonebottom, The Marrow bone mines, and Deep Docks.
Act I milestones include defeating Moss Mother, freeing Bell Beast, forging needle, and first Lace duel.

statement: Act II (The Mist and Threshold) spans Greymoor moors, the Belltower, and toxic Bile Lake precipices.
Act II culminates at the Southern Gate where Hornet destroys The Last Judge to breach the Citadel.
Act III spans Gilded City, Choral Chambers, Cogwork Vaults, Weavers' Cradle, and Mount Fay.
Act III culminates at Peak of Song where Hornet confronts Grand Mother Silk at the Loom of Pharloom.

statement: Ringing the Great Bell in the Belltower permanently silences lower shift alarms and alters enemy spawns.
The three-act structure embodies narrative architecture: spatial ascent mirrors psychological escalation.
Hornet evolves across the acts from an isolated escaped prisoner into an agent of revolutionary deicide.
Backtracking across acts functions indexically to reveal Hornet's impact upon the living populace.
All endings converge upon the inevitable collapse and unravelling of the theocratic Loom.
Silksong introduces Wishes: a quest system organized through task boards in towns and NPC dialogue.
Wishes span four primary categories: monster hunts (Cull), crafting (Forge), delivery, and rescue operations.
The Flea Caravan is a traveling troupe of acrobatic fleas led by the Flea Master in Bonebottom.
Rescuing scattered lost fleas across dangerous crags returns them to the encampment in Bonebottom.
Rescuing fleas expands the camp with new merchants, stat-boosting broths by Flea Cook, and music.
Completing Wishes rewards strings of Rosaries, shell shards, weapon tools, and Crest fragments.
The quest log records civilian requests, allowing Hornet to speak directly to citizens about personal lore.
Unlike Hallownest's dead necropolis, Pharloom is a densely populated society depending on Hornet's protection.
Completing Wishes proceduralizes an ethic of communal repair: clearing paths and mending frayed social ties.
The growing Flea Caravan provides tangible visual/acoustic evidence of grassroots social renewal.
The Wishes system enriches the world by balancing solitary acrobatics with communal mutual aid.
The survival of grassroots settlements after the Loom falls points toward autonomous self-governance.
Silksong replaces Soul and Charms with Silk Spools, Crest archetypes, and Craftable Tools.
Striking enemies with the needle gathers Silk, winding glowing thread into a circular spool.
When the spool is full, Bind wraps Hornet in thread, instantly restoring three masks of health.
Taking damage during the brief bind animation interrupts the healing and expends all gathered silk.
Crests are engraved emblems that alter Hornet's attack stance, kinetics, and tool slot capacity.
The Hunter Crest offers balanced martial kinetics, standard needle slashes, and agile mobility.
The Reaper Crest features wide sweeping scythe strikes, extended silk harvesting, and heavy stagger.
The Wanderer Crest optimizes traversal with lightning sprint speed and instant ledge-mantling.
The Weaver Crest empowers silk arts, accelerates spool recharge, and spawns thread spider minions.
The Architect Crest expands tool capacity, enhances deployable traps, and reinforces defense.
Tools crafted at benches span Straight Pins, Pimpillo Bombs, Sting Shards, and Rosary Cannons.
Crests transform the protagonist into an active artisan constructing specialized tactical loadouts.
